notes: DRAFT for scholarly review; nothing here is reviewed or published. English only: Arabic and Urdu are left for translators. Written from the Quran text in content/quran (Tanzil Uthmani) in the drafter's own words, and from nothing else: no hadith, no tafsir, no later tradition in the story texts. Chapters are a reading order, not a chronology the Quran claims. Where the Quran leaves a person unnamed or names only a title, the draft keeps them unnamed; identifications and later-tradition names appear only in the unknowns and uncertainties. Honorifics are added when the page is rendered.

claims.statement_en: The Quran says that the hands of Abu Lahab have perished, and that he has perished.
His wealth and what he earned did not avail him.
He will burn in a fire of flame.
His wife is mentioned as the carrier of firewood.
Her neck has a rope of palm fibre around it.

chapters.summary_md: The Quran says that the hands of Abu Lahab have perished, and that he has perished [c1]. His wealth and what he earned did not avail him [c2]. It says that he will burn in a fire of flame, and it mentions his wife as the carrier of firewood [c3][c4].
chapters.body_md: The Quran says that the hands of Abu Lahab have perished, and that he has perished [c1]. His wealth and what he earned did not avail him [c2]. He will burn in a fire of flame [c3]. His wife is mentioned as the carrier of firewood [c4]. Her neck has a rope of palm fibre around it [c5].
chapters.deep_md: The passage names him as Abu Lahab and gives no other name [c1]. It speaks of his wife in the last ayat, and the ayat do not say what the carrier of firewood refers to [c4][c5].
chapters.kids_md: The Quran says that Abu Lahab's wealth and what he earned did not help him [c2]. His wife is called the carrier of firewood [c4].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the passage says wealth and earnings did not avail him [c2]. Another is that the passage speaks of his wife as well as of him [c4].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established in these ayat: who Abu Lahab was, what his own name was, or why he is named in this way. Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: he is identified as an uncle of Muhammad, and his own name is given as Abd al-Uzza.
- Not established: the wife's name, or what the carrier of firewood means; the phrase can be read literally or figuratively.
- Not established: the occasion on which the passage was revealed; it names no event.
- Not established: what the rope of palm fibre signifies.

uncertainties_en: Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the man is identified with an uncle of Muhammad, his wife is given a name, and the occasion of the passage is told in later works.
Hadith to add later: reports about the occasion of the passage, with a named grader for each; none is used here.
